claims.claim: Across 300 injection payloads spanning 15 shell-metacharacter families ($(...), backticks, %VAR%, ${...}, ;, |, &&, >, command substitution nesting, CRLF injection, cmd /c invocation, touch), the workflow parameter sink forwards every payload to the child byte-identical (0 argv mismatches) and NO canary marker file was ever created - zero substitution anywhere in the pipeline.

Detector control: deliberately evaluating one payload through a real shell creates the canary marker (content 'pwned'), proving the probe can detect substitution when a shell is in the path; the reference sink then runs the same payload class and stays literal (marker absent, argv byte-identical).

negative_controls.description: A deliberately evaled payload demonstrates the canary fires exactly when a shell re-parses a parameter - the failure mode the unit guards against - while the list-argv sink never triggers it.

implementation.sink: subprocess list-argv spawn (shell=False, CreateProcess direct); child echoes received argv bytes as JSON
implementation.canary: every payload embeds a marker-creating command; the marker's absence after each run is the pass signal

signals.a: absence of the canary marker file after every sink call
signals.b: the recorded literal parameter value at the sink (child-received argv == sent payload, all 300)

observations.name: canary markers created across 300 payloads
observations.method: marker existence check after each list-argv sink call

observations.method: same payload class through a real shell

residual_unknowns.claim: The measured sink is the reference list-argv dispatch (the shape tools/lib/codex-invocation.mjs uses for child spawns); other call sites that interpolate parameters into shell strings elsewhere in the estate were not in this unit's sink list.
